notes: Austere Philadelphia commercial gallery, 41 works / 9 artists / 3 rooms, hung 18 Sep. The printer's spring wall-label press PDF reads as four separated blocks but is one continuous single-frame story in which the credit line is its own styled run the mapping readout drops (keeping its line break) so every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length and the validator still returns VALID. The 41-row registrar CSV is keyed by CATALOGUE number while the 44 photo files are named by ACCESSION under a different (year.sequence) scheme, and it carries 3 over-long artist-worded medium lines, 2 two-part dimensions, 2 credit lines against 39 blank cells, and one year given as a range. The 44 intern frames were shot over two days in two places (storeroom cool-flat against a mid-grey wall vs hung under warm track light), 40 works represented and one (C-029, a bronze at the foundry) has no frame at all, one work is shot twice as a full view plus a detail so 44 files never meant 44 works, three glazed works (C-008, C-019, C-020) carry the track lights in the varnish so a global lift raises the reflection, and several pale works sit at nearly the grey wall's value so a subject-crop mis-locks. The door's brushed-brass MARROW & VANE plate is photographed so the etched infill and the brushed ground run closest in value on the lit half and the ampersand and hairline rule are the thinnest strokes, so a trace clean at full canvas closes its counters and thins its rule at the size the checklist reproduces the mark on its own warm-grey ground. The installer hang-order txt double-lists two works across rooms (C-013 and C-036, first entries not struck) and leaves the last two Long Gallery positions to-be-confirmed. The director's desk note is the clean basis (title, dates, room names, credit convention, press line).

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's spring wall-label press PDF (single record, one label per page; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template — NO native layout file exists, this PDF is all that survives).

Document: single wall label, 105 x 148 mm PORTRAIT (A6), NO bleed box present (trim box = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded as subsets. One label per page. This is the exact file the gallery's printer ran for the spring show, and the look is to be kept exactly.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as four separated blocks, set small and high on the card with the lower two-thirds left as unprinted stock):
- Block 1 - TITLE, in the italic of the text face, about 11 pt.
- Block 2 - ARTIST and YEAR on one line, roman, about 9 pt (e.g. "Marisol Enback, 2023").
- Block 3 - MEDIUM on its own line then DIMENSIONS on the next, roman about 8 pt. Where a work carries one, a CREDIT line sits directly under the dimensions, italic about 7.5 pt.
- Block 4 - ACCESSION number alone at the foot of the printed block, about 6.5 pt.
Ink: Ink Black #1A1A18 on the Gallery White #F6F4EF card. No rule, no colour, no logo on the card - the restraint is the house style at this six-thousand-to-eighty-five-thousand-dollar band.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- Title, artist+year, medium, dimensions, the credit line and the accession are NOT six addressable text frames. They are ONE continuous text story in a SINGLE text frame, the apparent blocks separated only by line breaks and paragraph spacing.
- The CREDIT line is its own separately character-styled run inside that one story (an italic run). It is present on the spring card as a live example credit, reading exactly: "Courtesy of the artist and the Rittenhouse Trust".
- When this PDF is converted and the story is read back through the mapping readout, the credit run's TEXT is dropped from the readout while its LINE BREAK is kept. The reconstructed string therefore still looks well-formed (title / artist+year / medium / dimensions / [blank line] / accession), so nothing looks wrong - but every character offset computed AFTER the credit run is short by exactly the length of that omitted run. The validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those offsets, and the prepare step returns a completed-successfully message.
- Only a subset of the fields is actually present in the prepared template afterwards; which ones survived is reported in no response at all, and is visible only in the prepared document's own stories on a round-trip.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim box and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be produced from this file however the render is called; the handover must state this plainly rather than deliver a trim-only run as if it were bled.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as the content of the spring record, NOT as visible tokens on the card): TITLE | ARTIST | YEAR | MEDIUM | DIMENSIONS | CREDIT | ACCESSION.

Typography: one restrained institutional text face (a quiet old-style serif), title in its italic, at the small sizes above; measure about 78 mm, ranged left, the whole block sitting in the top third of the card. Carried over exactly as the printer set it, not reinterpreted.

assets.content:
MARROW AND VANE
Autumn exhibition — desk note from the director

SHOW
Title: GROUND AND FIGURE
Nine artists. Three rooms. Eighteen September through the second of November.
Private view: the evening of the seventeenth.

THE ROOMS, in this order
1. The Front Room
2. The Cabinet
3. The Long Gallery

THE ARTISTS
Marisol Enback, Tomás Grieve, Ilse Vanterpool, Petra Volková, Cyrus Mbeki, Della Hartley, Junot Sarraf, Wilhelmina Roa, Aksel Norr.

THE LABEL
One card per hung work. Title, artist, year, medium, dimensions, the credit where a work carries one, and our accession number small at the foot. No price on the card, no rule, no colour, no mark. Keep it as the printer set it in spring — the rooms are hung the same way and the labels should not look like a new decision. Small, quiet type high on the card, a lot of unprinted stock beneath it. The work carries the room.

CREDITS — set exactly as written, do not paraphrase
Most works carry no credit and take none. Where a work carries one it sits on its own line directly under the dimensions, in the form the registrar has entered it: "Courtesy of ..." or "Promised gift of ...". Two works in this show carry a credit; the rest do not.

THE CHECKLIST
The folded document for the desk and the press list. Same works, in hang order, three room sections, a small reference picture of each. We update it ourselves the week after the opening — two works will sell and one comes off the wall — so it has to stay something we can retype, not a picture of a list.

THE MARK
Our mark is the etched brass plate by the door: MARROW & VANE under a rule. On the checklist we want it as the mark itself, at its own small size, not a photograph of the brass.

PRESS
Press and image requests: press@marrowandvane.example — the registrar's desk, Wednesdays and Fridays.
